Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The Indians have taken their position. Mohammad Shami to bowl first! Two slips in place. Let's go....
...THE CHASE...

The damage is done and Sri Lanka should not think much about what happened. This is a really good pitch to bat on if the batters hold themselves down. The bowlers were taken to the cleaners. The scorecard speaks loudly. Sri Lanka were sloppy in the field. They dropped Kohli twice on 52 and 81 and it turned out to be very costly. Sri Lanka did well to end the innings well. They will be happy with that but the damage was done well earlier. Now then, someone has to anchor for the Lankans to sniff near the target. A mammoth chase. Can Sri Lanka get close?

Virat Kohli the man of the moment is up for a chat. He says he was mentally fresh after the break. Adds he was excited for the home season to start and the openers gave a good platform for others to follow. Shares that luck plays a big part and it went his way today. Reckons they have got 20-25 runs extra and he is happy with the score. Feels the due will be a big factor and their bowlers will get good practice to play in these tough conditions. Tells he is in his prime shape.

Massive score by India! Mission ODI World Cup is in full flow and the batters have turned up big! What a performance. It was a belter of a pitch and India made the most of it. Starting with Gill and Sharma wasting no time up front. Both went bang, bang and scored respective fifties. Gill fell first then the skipper followed. The openers scored at a quick rate and laid the platform for others. It was then the poster boy of India to notch his 73rd international hundred. He allowed the likes of Iyer and Rahul to launch but once they failed, Kohli took the baton in his hands and notch a big ton. King Kohli maneuvered his innings well and helped India get over 370.

It is time for the 50-over format. After a decent T20I series, it is time to shift focus on a format which is a little longer. Both the sides will use this series to prepare for the upcoming World Cup. The Indians have their big names back, players who will more or less be featuring in the mega event. Lanka on the other hand, will be going ahead with the same players who played the T20Is. Toss and teams in a bit...
... MATCH DAY ...

The fastest ride of the T20I format now comes to an end! The competition between India and Sri Lanka moves to the next face of the tour, as the two teams get ready to compete in a three-match ODI series, which will help them start their preparations for the 50-over World Cup which will be played later this year. The first ODI will be played at Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati. Hardik Pandya led India in the shortest format of the game with some key players being rested. The hosts were able to clinch the series by 2-1, and now, would be eyeing to transcend the same form in the 50-over format. Also, another thing for the Indian fans to cheer about is the return of some big names to the side. The top order comprises Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli and Suryakumar Yadav, with Shreyas Iyer, Hardik Pandya and KL Rahul making sure they have enough depth with the blade in the middle order. Also, it has been decided by the board to not rush Jasprit Bumrah into action and the speedster will skip this series. Mohammad Shami is likely to spearhead the attack with the likes of Mohammed Siraj, Arshdeep Singh and Umran Malik in the mix. While, it could be a reunion for the spin department as Kuldeep Yadav and Yuzvendra Chahal might work in tandem, with Washington Sundar and Axar Patel the other spinners in the squad. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will face a stern test against this Indian side which looks solid on paper but this ODI series will surely help them understand where they stand in this format. Sri Lanka will be hoping to challenge the opposition batters with their mixture of experience and youngsters in the bowling department. They also have a solid unit when it comes to putting up runs on the scoreboard, only if they are to put the application on display. Sri Lanka would be hoping to take an early lead in this series and put the hosts on the back foot. Although, it won't be an easy walk in the park for them. Will India be able to get an early lead in this series? Or will Sri Lanka be able to pull a rabbit out of the hat here? We shall find out together.
